title: CRLR/96/2012 of VIGYAN VIKRAM SHAH Vs MAHARAJA NARENDRA SHAH AND ANR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Delay Condonation Application No.604/2012
Stay Application No.605/2012
Urgency Application No.3289 of 2012
IN
Criminal Revision No.96 of 2012
Vigyan Vikram Shah
 ÖÖ. Revisionist
Versus
Maharaja Narendra Shah Charitable Trust & another
 ..Ö. Respondents
Dated: August 3, 2012
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta , J.
 Mr. L.K. Tiwari, Advocate, for the revisionist.
Mr. R.S. Bisht, Advocate, for respondent no.1.
Mr. M.A. Khan, AGA, for the State/respondent no.2.
Objections filed on behalf of respondent no.1 against the
delay condonation application are kept with the records.
Having heard the learned counsel for the parties on the
delay condonation application, the same is hereby allowed.
After hearing the learned counsel on behalf of both the
parties on the revision, it transpires that a complaint case
no.550 of 2009 was filed in the court of Judicial Magistrate,
Dehradun by respondent no.1- Maharaja Narendra Shah
Charitable Trust through Sri J.B. Joshi (Secretary and Trustee)
against the revisionist Vigyan Vikram Shah for the offences
under Section 380/447 IPC. Learned Magistrate, after recording
the statement of complainant and his witnesses under Sections
200 and 202 Cr.P.C. respectively, did not find any sufficient
cause for taking cognizance in the matter and, accordingly, he
rejected the complaint u/s 203 Cr.P.C. Feeling aggrieved, the
criminal revision no.216 of 2012 was filed in the court of

2
Sessions Judge which was adjudicated by the Additional
Sessions Judge vide judgment and order dated 23.5.2011,
whereby the said revision was allowed and the trial court was
directed to take cognizance in the matter. In compliance of the
directions of the revisional court, the trial court has taken
cognizance and thus, the revisionist, who is the accused, has
come up before the Court.
It has been pleaded on behalf of respondent that the
revisionist is not appearing before the court of Magistrate and
he has come up before this Court by way of instant revision.
On the other hand, the argument has been advanced on
behalf of revisionist that the revisional court allowed the
revision against him without affording any opportunity of
hearing. This argument has been refuted on behalf of
respondent that before passing order u/s 204 Cr.P.C., the
prospective accused has no locus standi to put up his
arguments before the revisional court. The argument, so
advanced by learned counsel for the respondent, would have
hold water in case the proceedings were pending only before the
Magistrate. But when learned Magistrate has refused to take
cognizance and dismissed the complaint u/s 203 Cr.P.C., then,
in case a revision is filed against him, the prospective accused
has every right to be impleaded as a party in the revision. The
above ratio has been propounded by the Honíble Apex Court in
a catena of decisions, particularly in the case of ìRaghu Raj
Singh Rousha Vs. Shivam Sundaram Promoters Private Limited
and another reported in (2009) 2 SCC 363î.
Apart from above, the Court feels that the revisional court
did not have any scope to issue directions to the Magistrate for
taking cognizance in the matter u/s 204 Cr.P.C. categorically.
At best, it should have remanded the matter with the directions
to the Magistrate to reconsider and re-evaluate the statement of
complainant and that of his witnesses.

3
Thus, on both the scores, the revision no.96 of 2012 has
merits. It is, accordingly, allowed. Impugned judgment and
order dated 23.5.2011 passed by the Additional Sessions
Judge/IV FTC, Dehradun in Criminal Revision No.216 of 2010,
Maharaja Narendra Shah Charitable Trust Vs. State, is hereby
overturned. The matter is remanded back to the Sessions
Judge, Dehradun, with the direction, either to hear the matter
himself or transfer to the same to any appropriate court.
Revisionist will be impleaded as a respondent in the said
revision and the same will thereafter be disposed of by
rendering a fresh opportunity of hearing to the parties. It is
further made clear that in pursuance of this judgment, any
proceedings issued by learned Magistrate, after taking
cognizance in the matter, are hereby quashed.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
03.08.2012
Rdang
